title: Cedar raised garden bed
summary: This cedar bed is 47 1/2 in long, 24 in wide and 11 in high. You cut twelve parts, attach them with deck screws, and fill the bed with soil.
priceNote: Example US home center prices (November 2026) with 7% sales tax. Replace them with the prices and the tax rate at your store.

home.name: Home center
home.note: Pick straight boards with few knots. Look along each edge before you buy it.

cedar-2x6.name: Cedar board
cedar-2x6.note: Buy planed boards. Rough boards are thicker, and the parts then do not fit.

cedar-4x4.name: Cedar post
cedar-4x4.note: Keep the offcut. It gives the posts for a second bed.

screw.name: Deck screw
screw.spec: #10 x 3 in, coated for outdoor use, star drive
screw.head: flat
screw.note: The box has a driver bit for the screws.

fabric.name: Landscape fabric
fabric.note: Optional. Use it only where weeds grow.

soil.name: Raised bed soil
soil.spec: mix for raised beds, 2 cu ft

tools.name: Drill bit set
tools.spec: 1/8 in drill bit and a countersink bit

cut-straight.name: Cut on the line

warn.text: Wear safety glasses. The saw can throw chips into your eyes.
Wear ear protection. A loud saw can hurt your ears.
Keep your hands 6 in from the blade. The blade can cut your fingers.
Stand to the side of the saw line. A saw that jumps back can hit you.
Support the board so that the cut stays open. A cut that closes on the blade makes the saw jump back toward you.
Do not lock or remove the lower blade guard. The guard covers the blade after the cut.

do: Set the blade depth 1/4 in more than the thickness of the board.
If you cut a post, set the blade to its full depth.
Put the board on the sawhorses, with the line near a sawhorse.
Put a second support under a long waste piece, near the line.
Do not cut between two sawhorses that are far apart.
Align the blade with the waste side of the line.
Let the saw reach full speed before it touches the wood.
Push the saw slowly along the line.
Let a short waste piece fall. Do not hold it.
Before you lift the saw, let the blade stop.
cut-straight.why: The blade removes {kerf} of wood. A cut on the waste side keeps the part at its full length.

pilot-hole.name: Drill a pilot hole

warn.text: Wear safety glasses. The bit can throw chips into your eyes.

do: Put a scrap block under the board at the mark.
Hold the drill at 90° to the face.
Drill through the board into the scrap block.
pilot-hole.why: A pilot hole gives the screw a path. Without it, the cedar can split near an end.

countersink.name: Countersink the hole

warn.text: Wear safety glasses. The bit can throw chips into your eyes.

do: Put the countersink bit in the pilot hole.
Drill until the cone is as wide as the screw head.
Remove the dust from the hole.
countersink.why: The cone lets the screw head sit flush with the face.

square-diagonals.name: Square a frame
do: Measure the frame from corner to corner.
Measure the other diagonal.
If the two lengths are not equal, push the long diagonal corners together.
Measure again until the two lengths are equal within 1/8 in.
square-diagonals.why: A square frame has two equal diagonals.

finish-wipe.name: Apply an oil finish

warn.text: Wear nitrile gloves. Oil on your skin can cause a rash.
Put used cloths flat outdoors to dry, or in a closed metal can of water. Oily cloths can catch fire.

do: Stir the oil for 1 minute.
Apply a thin coat with a lint-free cloth.
Rub the oil along the grain.
Wipe off the oil that stays on the face.
finish-wipe.why: A thin coat goes into the wood and dries. A thick coat stays sticky.

level-check.name: Level the bed
do: Put the spirit level on the top edge of a board.
Read the position of the bubble.
Turn the level end to end on the same spot.
Read the bubble again.
If the bubble is not between the lines, remove soil under the high end.
level-check.why: A good level shows the same reading in the two directions.

steps.title: Cut the parts

warn.text: Wear a dust mask. Cedar dust can cause asthma.

do: Put each board on the two sawhorses.
Mark each cut from the cut list.

do.t: Measure each length two times before you cut.

do: Cut each long board A and each short board B on the waste side of the line.
Cut each post C from two opposite faces.
Write the part letter on the inside face of each part.
steps.check: Make sure that you have four long boards A, four short boards B and four posts C.
steps.why: A 7 1/4 in circular saw cuts about 2 3/8 in deep. The post is 3 1/2 in thick, so you cut it from two faces.
steps.tip: Mark the post line on all four faces. The two cuts then meet.

steps.title: Drill the screw holes
do: Draw a line across each long board A, 3 1/4 in from each end.
Draw a line across each short board B, 1 3/4 in from each end.
Mark two holes on each line of a long board, 1 1/4 in from the edges.
Mark two holes on each line of a short board, 2 in from the edges.
Drill a 1/8 in pilot hole through the board at each mark.
Countersink each hole on the outside face.
steps.check: Make sure that each board has four holes.
steps.why: The screws from a long board and a short board go into the same post. Different heights keep the screws apart.

steps.title: Attach two long boards to two posts

view.note: The picture shows the bed upright.

warn.text: Wear safety glasses. The driver bit can slip and throw chips.
Hold the drill with two hands. A long screw that stops can twist your wrist.

do: Put two posts C on a flat surface, about 41 in apart.
Put two long boards A on the posts, edge to edge, with the outside faces up.
Align the ends of each post with the outer edges of the boards.
Move each post until it is 1 1/2 in from the ends of the boards.
Drive one screw through each hole into the posts.
steps.check: Make sure that each post is square to the boards.
steps.why: The gap at each end holds a short board B. The posts then sit inside the corners of the bed.
steps.tip: An offcut of cedar board is a good spacer: it is 1 1/2 in thick, the same as short board B.

steps.title: Attach the last long boards to two posts

view.note: The picture shows the bed upright, as it stands at the end.

warn.text: Wear safety glasses. The driver bit can slip and throw chips.
Hold the drill with two hands. A long screw that stops can twist your wrist.

do: Put the last two posts C on a flat surface, about 41 in apart.
Put the last two long boards A on the posts, with the outside faces up.
Align each post 1 1/2 in from the ends of the boards.
Drive one screw through each hole into the posts.
steps.check: Put the two assemblies face to face. Make sure that the posts are at the same positions.

steps.title: Attach the short boards at one end

warn.text: Wear safety glasses. The driver bit can slip and throw chips.
Hold the drill with two hands. A long screw that stops can twist your wrist.

do: Stand the two assemblies on their bottom edges, with the posts inside.
Move the assemblies until the outside faces are 24 in apart.
Put a short board B between the long boards at one end, against the posts.
Align the bottom edge of the short board with the bottom edges of the long boards.
Drive one screw through each hole into the posts.
Attach the second short board B above the first in the same way.
steps.check: Make sure that the short boards are flush with the ends of the long boards.
steps.tip: Ask a helper to hold the two assemblies upright.

steps.title: Attach the short boards at the other end

warn.text: Wear safety glasses. The driver bit can slip and throw chips.
Hold the drill with two hands. A long screw that stops can twist your wrist.

do: Put a short board B between the long boards at the bottom of the other end.
Measure the two diagonals of the bed from corner to corner.
If the diagonals are not equal, push the long diagonal corners together.
Drive one screw through each hole into the posts.
Attach the second short board B above the first in the same way.
steps.check: Make sure that the two diagonals are equal within 1/8 in.
steps.why: A square bed has two equal diagonals. The screws then keep that shape.

steps.title: Apply the oil

warn.text: When you sand, wear a dust mask. Cedar dust can cause asthma.

do: Sand the top edges and the outside corners with 80 grit.
Remove the dust with a dry cloth.
Do not apply oil to the inside faces.
Apply a thin coat of oil to the outside faces and the top edges.
After 15 minutes, wipe off the extra oil.
Wait 24 hours.
steps.check: Make sure that the oil is dry before you fill the bed with soil.
steps.why: Cedar lasts outdoors without a finish. The oil keeps the outside color longer, and no oil touches the soil.

steps.title: Put the bed on level ground

warn.text: Call 811 before you dig. Buried cables and pipes can be near the surface.

do: Mark an area on the ground 6 in larger than the bed on each side.
Remove the grass in the area with the spade.
Scrape the high spots flat.
Put the bed in the area.
Put the level on each long board and each short board.
If the bubble is not between the lines, remove soil under the high corner.
steps.check: Make sure that the bubble is between the lines on each top board.
steps.why: A level bed holds water evenly. On a slope, the water runs out at the low end.
steps.tip: The bed weighs about 40 lb. Ask a helper to carry it.

steps.title: Fill the bed with soil
do: If weeds grow in this area, cut a 4 ft length of landscape fabric.
If you use fabric, put it flat on the ground inside the bed.
Pour the soil into the bed.
Spread the soil flat with the spade.
Fill the bed to 1 in below the top edge.
Wet the soil with a hose.
steps.check: After the soil is wet, make sure that it is 1 in to 2 in below the top edge.
steps.why: Wet soil sinks a little. The gap at the top keeps the soil and the water in the bed.
steps.tip: The bed holds about 5 1/2 cu ft of soil. Three 2 cu ft bags fill it.
